items.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011
items.q: I had a great teacher, Frank Galime, he was the person who really kept me going for a long time

ctx.x: We’ll talk more about that. I’m wondering if you felt like a big fish in a small pond growing up in Oriskany? For those people who are watching this, Oriskany is like a little adjoining town to Utica.

Yeah. It’s not even a town it’s a village. But yeah, I mean in the town itself there really wasn’t that much going on. I mean we had the chorus and the band, and I had a great teacher, Frank Galime, he was the person who really kept me going for a long time, and then he introduced me to you, and also Jack Adams from Holland Patent. So simultaneously I had outside instruction, and that allowed me to go on to around to New York State NYSSMA competitions and I got involved, in chorus, I was singing in All- State…
Was your whole childhood in Oriskany?
